# Lecture 2 — transcript

¶1 Auzubillah Minashaitan Nirajeem

¶2 Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Rahim

¶3 Last week we had an introduction about what is irfan. And if you remember I had said that there are things in this world which we do not see and hear and there are things which we do not understand. And the Islamic Irfan or mysticism is to teach us how to see, hear and understand these things. Now you probably have read these verses from the quran very frequently because it comes up in different phases of the quran “lahum quloobul laa yafqahoona bihaa wa lahum a'yunul laa yubisiroona bihaa wa lahum aazaanul laa yasma'oona bihaa; ulaaa'ika kal an'aami bal hum adall; ulaaa'ika humul ghaafiloon” 7:179 they have heart by which they do not understand, they have eyes by which they do not see and they have ears by which they do not hear.

¶4 They are like animals and even worse. Now I ask you, animals have eyes and ears; do they not see and hear? I mean because here there is a comparison here between animals and those types of human beings who do not see, hear and understand. But animals do they not see and hear? They do, isn’t it? I mean certainly they could see while they walk and certainly they could hear because that’s why when we at them, when they hear a sound they run away. What is it that Allah is making comparison with? What we mentioned last time was that there is a machine inside the human being which has to translate what we see and hear to reach the reality.

¶5 What we see and what we hear are only at the surface. They are superficial. The reality of those things that we see and hear is only understood by some. Animals see and hear but they do not have that machine to translate it. We also see and hear, now the kuffar for example, they see and they hear and we tell them that you have eyes by which you do not see. They would laugh and tell us that we see better than you do. We see things in a more detailed and more artistic way than you see. However quran says, yes they see but they do not understand. Now this enigma of having and not having, listening and not listening, being and not being will come up inshaAllah in the course of these lessons and you will become familiar with the mysteries of mysticism of seeing, being and not being, having and not having.

¶6 What the verse of the quran wants to tell us is that of course you see and hear but you see and hear with your mind, your eyes which only give you a sight of it. What you do not see and do not translate, you have the machine or the soul but it doesn’t work. It is not working. It is dead and blind. This is what mysticism teaches us to do so that somehow it ignites the machine which is inside us to start working and once it starts working then of course the work of mystics begin and it’s the beginning of the move. Of course mysticism has a beginning and no end. Everyone says that mysticism has an end.

¶7 There is no end but it has a beginning. The beginning of it is when that machine starts to work and offer then of course you see the wonders of this world. There are 2 groups of people, one group who’s soul work and the other whose soul doesn’t work or don’t work at all. The former we call them “Urafaa”. Urafaa is the plural of Aarif. Aarif means someone who knows and therefore the other people are jahala or those who don’t know. They do not have the capability to know and understand. So we have 2 groups of people. Last week we had a mention of these people “urafaa” ie. Those who know. In hades and if you remember any verse of the Quran referring to a group of people who are different from us.

¶8 I’m not talking about prophets and immah. They are very special urafaa. Ordinary people not at the level of prophets and immah and you remember any verse of the quran talking about special group of people having different understanding than that ordinary mominoon. I’m not talking about kuffar. Ordinary mominoon of course they have an understanding but there are some special people with special understanding. They have a mention in the Quran. Can anybody remember any verse of the Quran which is referring to some people who are different from mominoon. We had mentioned about muqarrabun last week. There are a group of people who are called muqarrabun or those who are brought near. Of course muqarrabun are those who are brought near but Allah is not far away, isn’t it.

¶9 He is very near. So in what sense they are brought near, in a sense that probably some veil which was between ordinary people and Allah is taken away. They understand far better and that’s why they are muqarrab. This is the meaning of muqarrab. If you remember this is what we discussed last week about the grouping of the people being of 3 kinds. If you remember we had said that the muqarrabun are of 4 categories. These 4 categories are mentioned in Sura Nisa “Wa many-yuti'il laaha war Rasoola fa ulaaa'ika ma'al lazeena an'amal laahu 'alaihim”4:69 anyone who obeys Allah’s prophet they will be of those whom Allah has bestowed favour. I just want to highlight them. Some people have the favour of Allah.

¶10 What is favouring? Certainly it is not wealth or a strong body. It is something else. These groups who have favour, Allah says here they are prophets (nabiyyen), the truthful (siddiqeen), the witnesses (shohada). These 3 groups of course we cannot reach that level. It is very special. So those on whom Allah has bestowed favour who are muqarrabun, has a very ending category here and that is saleheen. Saleheen are those who deserve or those who have the capacity to be given this favour. For example about some prophets, Allah said why we made them prophets because they were from saleheen and therefore if someone is from saleheen, Allah will choose them to be siddiqeen and then nabi. It is only from this saleheen that Allah would choose the other 3 categories.

¶11 And it is from only these 2 that Allah would choose and these categories have some siddiqeen that Allah would choose nabiyeen. Now for example about Lut, Allah says “Wa adkhalnaahu fee rahmatinaa innahoo minas saaliheen” 21:75 we made him enter into our mercy which is the special mercy. He was from saaliheen. He deserved, he was in this category. This category of saaliheen of course are those people who understand better than us, who see and hear better than us. Is there any other verse which explains who the saaleheen are? Any other verse you remember in the quran? Sura Anfal, “Innamal mu'minoonal lazeena izaa zukiral laahu wajilat quloobuhum” 8:2 mominoon are those who when the name of Allah is mentioned, their heart trembles.

¶12 Is there anyone here whose heart trembles when he or she hears the name of Allah? Well, even if we have we are not going to reveal this secret. Anyhow, it is not ordinary mominoon. When Allah is mentioned their heart trembles. Now can anyone tell me how this happens? I mean what type of quality should a person have that when Allah’s name is mentioned their heart trembles. When I mention something to you and you get scared or you tremble or whatever. What type of attribute a person should have to get this type of feeling? You should have a feeling of experience like for example when I mentioned something that is very scary to me. You should have some sort of idea or experience about it and then you get scared or you become for example numb or something which you already know.

¶13 Therefore there are some mominoon who know Allah and that’s why when you mention his name, their heart trembles. There are different group of mominoon, isn’t it? They are not ordinary mominoon of course. Now what else do we have? Look at this verse, “Qad aflahal mu'minoon. Allazeena hum fee Salaatihim khaashi'oon” 23:1/2 these are the mominoon who are humble in their prayers. It is not me certainly and many of you might not be like this. But this is not us. Those who when they stand before Allah they feel that humbleness in their heart. And khaashi is someone who is broken. I mean it’s more than humbleness. It means that it experience something that makes you down inside yourself and a real momin of course this is a different type of momin than ordinary mominoon.

¶14 When they stand before Allah in salaah they break down. That is because of their experience that they have of Allah. Can Allah be experienced at all? This is what mysticism is all about. Can we have a way or a canal or a path to Allah? Now let’s go higher. Look at this verse in Sura Ale-Imran, it is one of the great verses of the quran for only people who have high knowledge can understand. “Shahidal laahu annahoo laa ilaaha illaa Huwa walmalaaa'ikatu wa ulul 'ilmi qaaa'imam bilqist; laaa ilaaha illaa Huwal 'Azeezul Hakeem” 3:18 There is no god but He: That is the witness of Allah, His angels, and those endued with knowledge. Allah has the knowledge of his own tawheed, isn’t it?

¶15 Now we also have the knowledge of tawheed but could we compare our knowledge of tawheed with Allah’s knowledge of his own tawheed? Of course not. He has the knowledge of his own tawheed and he witnesses that there is nothing but him. No god, no being beside him and the angels witness that as well. Angels witness that and so human being. Which human being? Wa ulul 'ilmi, those who are endued with knowledge. He is of course again, ulul ilam this is another expression of aarif, isn’t it? Urafaa, those who have maarifah, those who have knowledge they of course witness that tawheed of Allah. The concept of tawheed is very difficult if you want to think about it.

¶16 It is not as simple as just saying that there is no god but Allah. This is of course the simplest meaning that we understand but if you want to understand more and deeper then we of course we cannot live by our intellect. We have to start and ignite that machine inside us, the soul. It’s only that part of us that can grab tawheed and what’s the meaning of this verse. It’s only that part which understands. Of course we have heard that the verses of the Quran have layers of depth. Each verse of the Quran are 7 layers of depth and beneath each layer there are 70 layers of depth and beneath each 70 layer there are 700 layers of depth.

¶17 Of course we understand something from this verse and somebody may understand much much deeper. It’s the same thing, same meaning concept but understood different at different level. “Innamaa yakhshal laaha min 'ibaadihil 'ulamaaa” 35:28 of course this is a short translation of the whole verse. A part of the verse that we are talking about only those who are possessed of knowledge have fear of Allah. All of us here in a way fear Allah but we fear his punishment more than fearing himself. But there are some people who fear him and not his punishments. His heart is filled type of fear which we cannot explain. It’s not fear of punishment. It is something else. These are just a few examples of how some people are different and they are mentioned in the Quran and we cannot deny that.

¶18 Anyone can think about any other verse or any other expreson in the quran? Ulul Albah, those who have inner intellect. What about awliyaallah, the friends of god? “Alaa innaa awliyaaa'al laahi laa khawfun 'alaihim wa laa hum yahzanoon” 10:62 verily on the friends of Allah there are no fear, nor shall they grieve. So again it is group of people who are different from us. How someone can become a friend of Allah and connect to Allah very closely according to how we translate the term wali. There is one other verse in Surah Nahl, “Man 'amila saaliham min zakarin aw unsaa wa huwa mu'minun falanuhyiyannahoo hayaatan taiiyibat” 16:97 whoever is a momin and does good, amila saaliham comes from saleheen, isn’t it?

¶19 Whoever acts a saleeh or a good action will become a saleheen. It is whoever does that, whoever becomes from saleheen is a momin. We will give them a different type of life which is hayaatan taiiyibah, a clean and pure life. Taiiyibah because it is clean and pure from the filth of this world. They get aloof. They live in this world but they do not live in the filth of this world. They somehow transcend the worldly issues which other people are infected with. And this hayaatan taiiyibah is of course what mystics are after. They want to acquire this. I think this introduction would suffice as an introduction to tell us who mystics are and why they put themselves in so much hardship, lots of training and purification to find a glimpse and experience of Allah which of course the love has been put in their heart and that’s why they are glad to seek.

¶20 About awliyaAllah, I discussed last week and I will go through it very quickly. Now let’s go through the course properly and deal with some terminology. What I said up till now was just an introduction to get a glimpse of what irfan is about and what we are actually going to search in the course of these sessions. We have different terms here.

¶21 Irfan comes from maarifah. Maarifah is knowledge and understanding. This type of knowledge and practise is called irfan which means possessing maarifah of course we will discuss the difference between maarifah and ilm in ordinary sense although in religious terminolgy ilm and maarifah are used unanimously. There is no knowledge or ilm but maarifah of Allah. We usually call the knowledge of Allah, someone who has the knowledge of Allah has maarifah. And someone is having knowledge of the world matters having ilm from the maarifah. So that’s we call them irfan someone who possess this maarifah is called an aarif and the plural is urafaa.

¶22 It is also called Sufism. Now why its call Sufism is really breath-taking and there are many theories why these group of people we usually acquire such knowledge are called Sufi’s. The term sufiyah meaning practising Sufi practise was first used by Jami in 255AH in the 3^(rd) century but the very attribute given to people calling someone Sufi goes back in the 2^(nd) century. And the first person who was called Sufi was Abu Hashem al-Kufi. Some people say it comes from the Latin term “scientia” meaning knowledge but I don’t think it is. The best explanation is because these people were wearing a special type of woollen rough clothes and it is called “suf” and that’s why someone who actually wears it is called Sufi and sifiyah.

¶23 However Sufism which is not very much favoured especially by Shia and Sunni scholars because the early Muslim mystics many of them they borrowed concepts and practises from Sufis of other religion and other faith or even the faith which of those who were not monotheist. And because these practises came and some of them left their shariah all together and that’s why the term Sufi and sufiyah became a type of attribute which was not very much favoured by religious people. So even today if you say Sufi or sufiyah there hear something which you find in many Shia scholar books, lots of bad things about it and especially report some hades about people. The immah were against this Sufi and therefore the immah were against mysticism.

¶24 However we have to distinguish between the right and the wrong practise, right and wrong intention. However Sufism is another term used for urafaa and we can use or we can change it.

¶25 Another term used is mysticism which we have used here. This is from mystic. Usually Christian urafaa used mysticism because this actually deals with mystery. You know Christians faith is shrouded with mysteries especially the idea of takmeel because no one knows what faith mean. They favour this because they say the whole faith and understanding of god is a mystery. However we use it of course because of different reasons. We have concepts like tawheed and the other very tidy concept which everyone would understand of course at different levels. What more you go into that world of Allah the more wonders you see and the more mysterious it would become. Therefore it is a right term to use.

¶26 When you encounter that dignity and greatness of Allah you are mystified. So that’s why we use mysticism of course which is to deal with bewilderness and mystification and another term which comes from ancient Greek, agnosticism from agnostic which is to do with knowledge and I think if you a want to be exact we use the term agnosticsism for Islamic Irfan because Islamic Irfan deals with maarifah of Allah. Knowledge and of course love of Allah. We will discuss this later on. So mystics in Islam they emphasis on maarifah and some mystics emphasis on love and of course these 2 hand in hand with each other because the more you find maarifah of Allah the more you find that love in your heart.

¶27 The more you have love for Allah means more maarifah you have for Allah. You do not love him because you do not know him. We usually get like people or love people if you know some characteristics or features of them. I mean otherwise out of the blue you cannot fall in love. And those people who fall in love with Allah they know some features if they have any features. If you have any features or use it metaphorically they know some features of Allah which makes them more productive. So love and maarifah go hand in hand. And the best expression for Islamic Irfan is agnosticism. How it highlights mysticism because it’s a mysterious world. When you enter this world of maarifah we become mystical.

¶28 I mean we become more bewildered up to the pace of one who uses it.

¶29 When we say knowledge, what type of knowledge? Of course we have different types of knowledge. Usually the philosophers and the mystics categorise knowledge in2 parts: Knowledge that you have acquired. It could be acquired by reasoning or senses. This is called Ilmul husul. Husul means to acquire. What you acquire from outside. You get some concepts and analyse those concepts. Of course the concepts which are with you of course not acquired, they are with you. However you acquire what corresponds to those concepts from outside. So this is one type of knowledge. The other type of knowledge is called knowledge with pleasant ie ilmul khuzu. It means you don’t get the concepts. You don’t need any means to acquire it.

¶30 It is with you inside your soul. Mysticism is defined as the urge to reach out to the infinite by ilmul khuzu but how? Of course I am rushing forward because these are very difficult concepts. However does anyone of you have knowledge of ilmul khuzu type? Your own self. Ok because is very difficult as some of us don’t know about ourselves. We don’t know that our selves exist at all. We really don’t know that we exist. We are ignorant of that. But that’s true. That is the most important ilmul khuzu that we have. Anything else apart from ourselves? It is created inside and that knowledge comes from within. It doesn’t acquire from outside. No one can know by … It’s impossible.

¶31 It’s a very vague idea that we have for Allah inside us. Very simple example is hunger. When you feel hunger, I mean your soul feels it. I say your soul because it realises and understands it and have knowledge of it. It comes from within. Anxiety, it is something that you experience from very inside of yourself. Of course there is a cause for it but that cause is not what that feeling is. Now when I look at this for example there is a picture of this in my mind. That image is because of it. Although even that image is present in my mind and it is acquired because of this. However if this makes me anxious, although it is because of this but that anxiety comes from somewhere inside my soul by invoking other conflicts of life.

¶32 The knowledge which is present is something which is totally grasped and there is no missing of it. When you feel hungry, you really feel hunger. I might be false hunger but you feel something which is very real and that’s why it drives you or pain when you feel pain. This feeling comes from ilmul khusu. However if you want to know how it confuses is ilmul khusu. You cannot concentrate and feel that how it confuses you. You cannot do it. It is not possible. For some people it’s possible but for ordinary people it’s not possible. Everybody would not have the same knowledge with present. Yes, of course that what the mystics are after. They want the knowledge with present without development without any effort.

¶33 We have this knowledge with present with regards to some of our basic feelings but not all. When it comes to outside us, we don’t have that knowledge. It has to be acquired. There is a line of poem from Imam Ali which says, there is no masqook knowledge unless there is a masmoon ie. Inner knowledge. I have forgotten the poetry at the moment. However it is important to know that when for example your body moves towards an attitude which instigates hunger, your soul instantly without exerting any pressure will feel that hunger. That is ilmul khuzu. But you can never do it something that is outside you. You can never try, concentrate and feel that how this confusion is made.

¶34 You cannot. Usually for us ilmul khuzu is outside us and ilmul khusu is what is inside us. Can we somehow bring this to know? If you can do that then it is over. You cannot know god by ilmul khusu. It’s not possible. You just get the feeling and awareness. You just look at the sky and say that this should have a creator. How you want to find who that creator is? Can you concentrate, look at the sky and find who the creator is? You can’t do it at this stage but inshallah by the end of this course. These 2 types of knowledge is a theme of philosophy. Ilmul khusuli is received by aql which is called theoretical intellect.

¶35 We have aql which is called theoretically intellect by which we reason, we understand and argue. The argument, reasoning and analysing is right ilm which is knowledge of course. And that is like philosophy of course in respect to our discussion or science. The subject matter is different but the type of argument and reasoning is the same. So theoretical intellect is like ilm which is philosophy and science. We are dealing here with different types of knowledge not that knowledge that comes from analysis or argument or reasoning if provided. It is a knowledge which comes from human sight. We will deal about this later on. It might be vague at the moment but inshaAllah during the session we will discuss this further.

¶36 If you want to make a difference between ilm and maarifah, religious text says that ilm and maarifah is the same thing. But for us just to make a difference between these 2, ilm aims at understanding. It is limited to realm of time and space. And to understand things you have to be limited. You have to categorise, isn’t it? Every knowledge and science at the beginning they categorise things. They define, when you define something you limit it and that’s why in Arabic it’s called “Hadd”. When you finish something its hudood. Hudood is of course if you want to define you have to limit. For example you say haiwan-e-natiq. You put limits on it. So end these with limitations that how we can define.

¶37 Now what about maarifah? It doesn’t aim at understanding rather it aims at arriving because it is ilmul khuzul. You have to arrive at it. You arrive at hunger. You don’t try to understand hunger, so you just feel at arrival. It is beyond time and space. It aims at inside and self-purification and it rewards limitations. You have to put them in relation with each other by this type of understanding. Of course this will enter our soul and do purification. That’s how the machine which is rough is polished. Purification is actually polishing the soul so that it starts working. It is rough. It’s not working you have to set it and work, to start it and it would start after you have started purification.

¶38 What mysticism is about? It is to arrive taqwa and not to define god. Defining god is limited. In Nahjul Balagha we have that whoever defines god has limitations. We cannot define god. He only can arrive at him. And arriving at him of course has a very long story because when mystics say that when you arrive at Allah then that’s the beginning to move in the world of wonders and inshaAllah we continue next week.

¶39 Wa sallahu ala mohammadin wa aale hittahereen.
